questions.q:
Statement I: Staggered conformation of ethane is more stable than the eclipsed conformation.
Statement II: The torsional strain in staggered conformation is more.
Read the above statements and choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation: The staggered conformation is indeed more stable (Statement I true), but it has the least torsional strain, not more — the eclipsed conformation has greater torsional strain, so Statement II is false.

questions.q: The number of chain isomers possible for the hydrocarbon with molecular formula C$_5$H$_{12}$ is
questions.explanation: C$_5$H$_{12}$ has three chain isomers: n-pentane, isopentane (2-methylbutane) and neopentane (2,2-dimethylpropane).

questions.q: The compound with molecular formula C$_{20}$H$_{42}$ is
questions.explanation: An alkane C$_n$H$_{2n+2}$ with n = 20 is eicosane, C$_{20}$H$_{42}$.

questions.q: Which of the following is not an aromatic compound? [Structures shown: (1) cyclopentadienyl anion, a five-membered ring bearing a negative charge; (2) a six-membered ring cation drawn with only two double bonds and a positive charge, not fully conjugated around the ring; (3) tropylium cation, a seven-membered ring bearing a positive charge; (4) phenanthrene, three fused benzene rings]
options: Six-membered ring cation shown with only two double bonds (not fully conjugated)
questions.explanation: The cyclopentadienyl anion, tropylium cation and phenanthrene are all fully conjugated cyclic systems with 4n+2 π-electrons (aromatic); the six-membered ring cation shown is not fully conjugated and does not satisfy Hückel's rule, so it is non-aromatic.

questions.q: The IUPAC name of the given organic compound is HC$\equiv$C-CH=CH-CH=CH$_2$
questions.explanation: Numbering from either end gives the same locant set {1,3,5} for the multiple bonds; when locant sets tie, the double bond ('ene', cited first) is given the lower locants, so numbering from the CH$_2$ end gives hexa-1,3-dien-5-yne.

questions.q: Among the following, identify the compound that is not an isomer of hexane. [Structures: (1) CH$_3$-CH(CH$_3$)-CH$_2$-CH$_2$-CH$_3$; (2) CH$_3$-CH$_2$-CH(CH$_3$)-CH$_2$-CH$_3$; (3) CH$_3$-CH$_2$-CH$_2$-CH$_2$-CH$_2$-CH$_3$; (4) a four-membered ring (cyclobutane) with an ethyl substituent, i.e. ethylcyclobutane]
options: Ethylcyclobutane (a cyclobutane ring with an ethyl substituent)
questions.explanation: Options 1-3 are all branched or straight-chain isomers of hexane (C$_6$H$_{14}$); ethylcyclobutane is a cyclic compound with formula C$_6$H$_{12}$, so it is not an isomer of hexane.

questions.q: But-1-yne on reaction with dil. H$_2$SO$_4$ in presence of Hg$^{2+}$ ions at 333 K gives [structures shown: (A) butan-2-one CH$_3$COCH$_2$CH$_3$; (B) butanal CH$_3$CH$_2$CH$_2$CHO; (C) but-3-en-2-one CH$_2$=CHCOCH$_3$; (D) but-3-enal CH$_2$=CHCH$_2$CHO]
questions.explanation: Hg$^{2+}$-catalysed Markovnikov hydration of the terminal alkyne but-1-yne gives an enol that tautomerises to the ketone butan-2-one.

questions.q: In the given sequence of reactions, identify 'P', 'Q' and 'S' respectively. CH$_2$=CH$_2$ $\xrightarrow{P}$ CH$_2$Br-CH$_2$Br $\xrightarrow{Q}$ CH$_2$=CH-Br; also CH$_2$=CH-Br $\xrightarrow{R}$ CH$\equiv$CH $\xrightarrow{S}$ C$_6$H$_6$
options: HBr, Alc.KOH, NaNH$_2$, Red hot iron tube
Br$_2$, Alc.KOH, NaNH$_2$, Red hot iron tube
questions.explanation: Ethene adds Br$_2$ to give 1,2-dibromoethane (P = Br$_2$), which on dehydrohalogenation with alcoholic KOH (Q) gives bromoethene; NaNH$_2$ then gives acetylene, which cyclotrimerises over a red-hot iron tube (S) to give benzene.

questions.q: IUPAC name of the compound H$_3$C(H$_3$C)C=C(CH$_3$)CH$_3$ is
questions.explanation: The compound (CH$_3$)$_2$C=C(CH$_3$)$_2$ is a four-carbon chain (but-2-ene) with methyl substituents at C-2 and C-3, so its IUPAC name is 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene.

questions.q: Among the following: I. Benzene, II. Naphthalene, III. Cyclopentane, IV. Cyclopentadienyl anion, V. Cyclooctatetraene. The set which represents aromatic species is
questions.explanation: Benzene and naphthalene are aromatic (planar, cyclic, fully conjugated, obeying Huckel's 4n+2 rule), and the cyclopentadienyl anion is aromatic with 6 pi-electrons; cyclopentane is not conjugated and cyclooctatetraene is non-planar (tub-shaped) and non-aromatic.

questions.q: Arrange benzene, n-hexane and ethyne in decreasing order of their acidic behaviour
questions.explanation: Acidity of C–H bond increases with s-character: sp (ethyne) > sp$^2$ (benzene) > sp$^3$ (n-hexane), giving ethyne > Benzene > n-hexane.

questions.q: Peroxide effect is observed with the addition of HBr but not with the addition of HI to unsymmetrical alkene because
options: H-I bond is stronger that H-Br and is not cleaved by the free radical
H-I bond is weaker than H-Br bond so that iodine free radicals combine to form iodine molecules
Bond strength of HI and HBr are same but free radicals are formed in HBr
questions.explanation: Since the H–I bond is weaker, iodine free radicals formed recombine to give I$_2$ (an exothermic, favourable process) instead of continuing the radical chain, so the peroxide effect is not observed with HI.

questions.q: [2-ethyl-1-nitrobenzene ring] $\xrightarrow{Br_2, UV\ light}$ A. The compound A (major product) is [benzylic bromination at the ethyl CH$_2$ group]
options: 3-Bromo-4-ethyl-1-nitrobenzene (Br on ring, ortho to the ethyl group)
questions.explanation: Br$_2$/UV light causes free-radical substitution at the more stable benzylic position, replacing an H on the CH$_2$ adjacent to the ring to give the benzylic bromide, CH(Br)CH$_3$.

questions.q: Identify 'X' in the following reaction: benzene + 6Cl$_2$ (excess) $\xrightarrow[\text{dark, cold}]{\text{Anhydrous AlCl}_3}$ X + 6HCl
options: Hexachlorobenzene (all six ring H replaced by Cl)
questions.explanation: Release of 6 mol HCl means all six ring hydrogens undergo electrophilic substitution by Cl$_2$/AlCl$_3$, giving hexachlorobenzene (aromatic ring retained).

questions.q: 2-butyne is reduced to trans-but-2-ene using
questions.explanation: Dissolving-metal reduction with sodium in liquid ammonia reduces alkynes to the trans (E) alkene.

questions.q: Identify the following compound which exhibits geometrical isomerism :
questions.explanation: But-2-ene (CH$_3$-CH=CH-CH$_3$) has two different groups on each doubly bonded carbon, allowing cis-trans (geometrical) isomerism; the others do not have a suitable C=C.

questions.q: The reagent 'X' used for the following reaction R-C$\equiv$CR' + H$_2$ $\xrightarrow{X}$ cis-alkene is
questions.explanation: Partially poisoned Pd catalyst (Pd/C, as used in Lindlar-type hydrogenation) adds H$_2$ syn to an alkyne, giving the cis-alkene, whereas Na/liquid NH$_3$ gives the trans-alkene.

questions.q: For the preparation of Alkanes, aqueous solution of sodium or potassium salt of carboxylic acid is subjected to
questions.explanation: In Kolbe's electrolytic method, electrolysis of the aqueous sodium/potassium salt of a carboxylic acid produces an alkane at the anode.

questions.q: Toluene reacts with halogen in presence of Iron (III) chloride giving ortho and para halo compounds. The reaction is
questions.explanation: FeCl$_3$ generates an electrophile that substitutes a ring hydrogen of toluene — a classic electrophilic aromatic substitution.

questions.q: Electrophile that participates in nitration of benzene is
questions.explanation: In nitration of benzene, conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ and HNO$_3$ generate the nitronium ion, NO$_2^+$, which is the actual electrophile.

questions.q: Number of possible alkynes with formula C$_5$H$_8$ is
questions.explanation: The three possible alkynes of formula C$_5$H$_8$ are pent-1-yne, pent-2-yne and 3-methylbut-1-yne.

questions.q: Identify 'Q' in the following sequence of reactions: cyclohexyl methyl ketone (ring with -COCH$_3$) $\xrightarrow{\text{PCl}_5}$ P $\xrightarrow[\text{excess}]{\text{NaNH}_2}$ Q [Options are ring substituted with: (1) -CH=CH$_2$ (vinyl), (2) =CH$_2$ (exocyclic alkene), (3) -C$\equiv$CH (ethynyl), (4) -COCH=O]
questions.explanation: PCl$_5$ converts the ketone C=O into a gem-dichloride (P); excess NaNH$_2$, a strong base, then causes double dehydrohalogenation to give a terminal alkyne, ring-C$\equiv$CH (Q).

questions.q: Which of the following compound possesses the "C – H" bond with the lowest bond dissociation energy?
questions.explanation: Homolysis of a benzylic C-H bond in toluene gives a resonance-stabilised benzyl radical, which lowers its bond dissociation energy below that of aromatic, primary or secondary C-H bonds in the other options.

questions.q: The correct statement is
options: It is easier to hydrogenate benzene when compared to cyclohexene.
Hydrogenation of benzene to cyclohexane is an endothermic process.
One mole each of benzene and hydrogen when reacted gives 1/3 mole of cyclohexane and 2/3 mole unreacted hydrogen.
Cyclohexadiene and cyclohexene cannot be isolated with ease during controlled hydrogenation of benzene.
questions.explanation: Due to its aromatic stability (resonance/delocalisation energy), benzene is harder to hydrogenate than cyclohexene, and hydrogenation is exothermic (releases heat); the intermediate cyclohexadiene/cyclohexene cannot be isolated on controlled hydrogenation of benzene since once hydrogenation begins it proceeds rapidly to cyclohexane.

questions.q:
X $\xrightarrow[(Reductive)]{Ozonolysis}$ Y + Z

Y can be obtained by Etard's reaction, Z undergoes disproportionation reaction with concentrated alkali. X could be

[four substituted styrenes: (1) C$_6$H$_5$-CH=C(CH$_3$)$_2$, (2) C$_6$H$_5$-CH=CH-CH$_3$, (3) C$_6$H$_5$-CH=CH$_2$, (4) C$_6$H$_5$-C≡CH]
questions.explanation: Etard's reaction converts toluene to benzaldehyde (Y); reductive ozonolysis of styrene (C$_6$H$_5$-CH=CH$_2$) gives benzaldehyde (Y) and formaldehyde (Z), and formaldehyde undergoes the Cannizzaro (disproportionation) reaction with concentrated alkali.

questions.q: Cycloalkane formed when 1, 4-dibromopentane is heated with Sodium is
questions.explanation: Intramolecular Wurtz coupling joins C1 and C4 of pentane, forming a 4-membered ring with the C5 methyl group as a substituent, i.e., methylcyclobutane.

questions.q: Methane can be converted into Ethane by the reactions
options: Chlorination followed by the reaction with alcoholic KOH.
Chlorination followed by the reaction with aqueous KOH.
questions.explanation: CH$_4$ is chlorinated to CH$_3$Cl, which undergoes the Wurtz reaction with Na to give ethane (C$_2$H$_6$).

questions.q: Conversion of benzene to acetophenone can be brought by
questions.explanation: Benzene reacts with CH$_3$COCl/AlCl$_3$ in a Friedel-Crafts acylation to give acetophenone.

questions.q: Least energetic conformation of cyclohexane is
questions.explanation: The intended correct answer is the chair conformation (lowest energy form of cyclohexane); the option is misprinted as 'Chain conformation', so KEA awarded a grace mark to all candidates.

questions.q: 20 ml of methane is completely burnt using 50 ml of oxygen. The volume of the gas left after cooling to room temperature is
questions.explanation: CH$_4$+2O$_2\rightarrow$CO$_2$+2H$_2$O; 20 ml CH$_4$ needs 40 ml O$_2$, leaving 10 ml O$_2$ unused, plus 20 ml CO$_2$ formed (water condenses on cooling) = 30 ml total gas left.

questions.q: 100 ml of 0.1 M acetic acid is completely neutralized using a standard solution of NaOH. The volume of Ethane obtained at STP after the complete electrolysis of the resulting solution is
questions.explanation: Moles of CH$_3$COONa formed = 0.01. Kolbe electrolysis: 2CH$_3$COO$^-\rightarrow$C$_2$H$_6$+2CO$_2$+2e$^-$, giving 0.005 mol ethane = $0.005\times22400=112$ ml at STP.

questions.q: Which one of these is NOT TRUE for benzene?
options: There are three carbon-carbon single bonds and three carbon-carbon double bonds.
It forms only one type of monosubstituted product.
The bond angle between carbon-carbon bonds is 120$^0$.
Heat of hydrogenation of benzene is less than the theoretical value.
questions.explanation: All six C-C bonds in benzene are equivalent due to delocalization (bond length about 1.39 Å, between single and double bond lengths), so it does not literally have three single and three double bonds.

questions.q: Ethyl benzene CANNOT be prepared by ..................
questions.explanation: The Wurtz reaction couples two alkyl halides and cannot attach an alkyl group to an aryl halide; Wurtz-Fittig, Friedel-Crafts alkylation and Clemmensen reduction (of acetophenone) can all give ethylbenzene.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the most energetic conformation of cyclohexane?
questions.explanation: The stability order is chair < twist-boat < boat < half-chair, so the half-chair conformation has the highest energy.

questions.q: Which one of the following is an intermediate in the reaction of benzene with $CH_3Cl$ in the presence of anhydrous $AlCl_3$?
options: the arenium (cyclohexadienyl) cation formed by attack of the electrophile on the benzene ring
questions.explanation: $AlCl_3$ abstracts $Cl^-$ from $CH_3Cl$ to generate the electrophile $CH_3^+$ (as an $AlCl_4^-$ complex), which then attacks benzene.

questions.q: Which one of these is NOT true for benzene?
options: There are three carbon-carbon single bonds and three carbon-carbon double bonds.
It forms only one type of monosubstituted product.
The bond angle between the carbon-carbon bonds is 120$^0$.
The heat of hydrogenation of benzene is less than the theoretical value.
questions.explanation: Due to resonance/delocalization all six C-C bonds in benzene are equivalent (bond order 1.5), so describing three fixed single and three fixed double bonds is not true.

questions.q: A dibromo derivative of an alkane reacts with sodium metal to form an alicyclic hydrocarbon. The derivative is ...............
questions.explanation: 1,4-dibromobutane undergoes intramolecular Wurtz (Freund) reaction with Na to give cyclobutane, an alicyclic hydrocarbon.

questions.q: Which one of the following conformations of cyclohexane is the least stable?
questions.explanation: The half-chair conformation has the highest torsional and steric strain among cyclohexane conformations, making it the least stable.

questions.q: In electrophillic aromatic substitution reaction, the nitro group is meta directing because it
options: increases electron density at meta position
increases electron density at ortho and para positions
decreases electron density at ortho and para positions
decreases electron density at meta position
questions.explanation: The strongly electron-withdrawing -NO$_2$ group decreases electron density at the ortho and para positions (by resonance and induction), leaving the meta position comparatively favoured for electrophilic attack.

questions.q: The electrophile involved in the sulphonation of Benzene is
questions.explanation: In sulphonation of benzene with fuming sulphuric acid, the electrophile is SO$_3$.

questions.q: The carbon-carbon bond length in Benzene is
questions.explanation: Benzene's C-C bond length (~139 pm) lies between the single bond of ethane (154 pm) and the double bond of ethene (134 pm), due to delocalisation.
